searchText: <@!543900561460822016> have you folks started thinking about the receipt of 1559 txs? Maybe the current one is fine, but maybe it would make sense to include something like the "effective fee" I mean, that can be inferred from the tx and the block's base fee But perhaps it should be included in the receipt too? Are you wanting it in the receipt object or just to be returned from the RPC? What is the difference? The original 1559 spec had effective tip as an element in the receipt object. The value was serialized and hashed into the receipt trie root. We removed it because the value can be computed. I believe it was decided to return the value via the json-rpc. I’m guess the spec doesn’t have this element? Oh, I see what you mean, it's not included at the protocol level And no, the spec doesn't mention the RPC at all ah okay i am remembering now - we were thinking of having transaction objects in the rpc return their effective gas price but that wouldn't include receipts Does that make sense? You can have a tx object from a tx that is not mined, and therefore you can't know the effective gas price I think it makes more sense to have it in the receipt I agree, receipt is where this type of information lives currently for legacy transactions. Like logs (derived data) are in the receiipt. but you can't compute an effective gas price for tx if it isn't mined, because it is dependent on the block's base fee I suspect we may all be saying the same thing. That's what I'm saying too? 😅 Haha yeah Effective gas price should be included in the `eth_getTransactionReceipt` JSON-RPC response. and not `eth_getTransactionBy*`? Correct. `eth_getTransactionBy*` currently returns the transaction object, not derived data about the transaction's execution. it also returns `blockHash` and `blockNumber` i think it should return `effectivePrice` Yeah, it isn't 100% consistent, but *most* additional data is in the receipt. i don't have a strong opinion about the receipt, but there is currently no fee info in the receipt so it seems less intuitive I wouldn't be terribly against changing the `eth_getTransactionBy*` functions to return additional data like logs and such *when available*, but currently they are pretty narrowly focused (minus a couple oddities). i would be for changes like that i think we can start with `effectiveTip` in the tx object? `blockHash`, `blockNumber`, `from`, `transactionIndex` are the only things that aren't actually in the hashed data of a transaction. `getTransactionReceipt` includes all of that plus a bunch of derived data (some of which is actually in the receipt, some which is not). I think there's no fee info right now because it wasn't needed. But if you think of the receipt as containing "information that can only be computed after mining the tx", like the gas used, then it makes sense to have the effective fee there ~~A lot~~ Most of the current JSON-RPC endpoints have somewhat random/arbitrary data that was asked for or needed by developers for some task circa 2016. I do feel that this data (effective fee) is more appropriate in the receipt, even though the transaction object is not internally consistent with its named function. I also feel that including blockNumber/hash in the tx object was a mistake in retrospect, so I wouldn't add more stuff like that `from` seems ok because it's derived from the same data in the tx I can get on board with that one. updated with the `effectiveGasPrice` as a return value on `eth_getTransactionReceipt`: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/206 What would `eth_getBlockByNumber` return as `baseFee` for blocks before the hardfork? Options that come to mind are: 1) Don't show this property 2) Use a `baseFee` of 0 3) Use `null` Option 1 wouldn't be very consistent, since transactions pre-Berlin return a `type` value of 0 I think using a `baseFee` of 0 makes sense (no fee is being burned), but I don't know if that could cause issues or be misleading i don't think transactions pre-berlin are supposed to show type value of 0? Check this ``` curl -s -X POST --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_getTransactionByHash","params":["0x8cd030cb5c760d76badf6e44b87b00210219a2180f044376f2ed3041d1f7e27b"], "id": 1}' URL -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq .result.type ``` This is geth you’re seeing this? Yes

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: <@!543900561460822016> have you folks started thinking about the receipt of 1559 txs? Maybe the current one is fine, but maybe it would make sense to include something like the "effective fee"

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: I mean, that can be inferred from the tx and the block's base fee

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: But perhaps it should be included in the receipt too?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: Are you wanting it in the receipt object or just to be returned from the RPC?

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: What is the difference?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: The original 1559 spec had effective tip as an element in the receipt object. The value was serialized and hashed into the receipt trie root. We removed it because the value can be computed. I believe it was decided to return the value via the json-rpc. I’m guess the spec doesn’t have this element?

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: Oh, I see what you mean, it's not included at the protocol level

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: And no, the spec doesn't mention the RPC at all

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: ah okay i am remembering now - we were thinking of having transaction objects in the rpc return their effective gas price

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: but that wouldn't include receipts

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: Does that make sense? You can have a tx object from a tx that is not mined, and therefore you can't know the effective gas price

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: I think it makes more sense to have it in the receipt

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I agree, receipt is where this type of information lives currently for legacy transactions.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Like logs (derived data) are in the receiipt.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: but you can't compute an effective gas price for tx if it isn't mined, because it is dependent on the block's base fee

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I suspect we may all be saying the same thing.

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: That's what I'm saying too? 😅

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: Haha yeah

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Effective gas price should be included in the `eth_getTransactionReceipt` JSON-RPC response.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: and not `eth_getTransactionBy*`?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Correct.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `eth_getTransactionBy*` currently returns the transaction object, not derived data about the transaction's execution.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: it also returns `blockHash` and `blockNumber`

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i think it should return `effectivePrice`

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Yeah, it isn't 100% consistent, but *most* additional data is in the receipt.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i don't have a strong opinion about the receipt, but there is currently no fee info in the receipt so it seems less intuitive

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I wouldn't be terribly against changing the `eth_getTransactionBy*` functions to return additional data like logs and such *when available*, but currently they are pretty narrowly focused (minus a couple oddities).

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i would be for changes like that

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i think we can start with `effectiveTip` in the tx object?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `blockHash`, `blockNumber`, `from`, `transactionIndex` are the only things that aren't actually in the hashed data of a transaction.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `getTransactionReceipt` includes all of that plus a bunch of derived data (some of which is actually in the receipt, some which is not).

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: I think there's no fee info right now because it wasn't needed. But if you think of the receipt as containing "information that can only be computed after mining the tx", like the gas used, then it makes sense to have the effective fee there

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: ~~A lot~~ Most of the current JSON-RPC endpoints have somewhat random/arbitrary data that was asked for or needed by developers for some task circa 2016.  I do feel that this data (effective fee) is more appropriate in the receipt, even though the transaction object is not internally consistent with its named function.

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: I also feel that including blockNumber/hash in the tx object was a mistake in retrospect, so I wouldn't add more stuff like that

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: `from` seems ok because it's derived from the same data in the tx

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I can get on board with that one.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: updated with the `effectiveGasPrice` as a return value on `eth_getTransactionReceipt`: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/206

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content:
What would `eth_getBlockByNumber` return as `baseFee` for blocks before the hardfork? Options that come to mind are:

1) Don't show this property
2) Use a `baseFee` of 0
3) Use `null`

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: Option 1 wouldn't be very consistent, since transactions pre-Berlin return a `type` value of 0

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: I think using a `baseFee` of 0 makes sense (no fee is being burned), but I don't know if that could cause issues or be misleading

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i don't think transactions pre-berlin are supposed to show type value of 0?

